summary.headline: Zen Technologies Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to Rs.141.6 Cr (vs Rs.158.2 Cr YoY) and operational EBITDA margin to 27.3%, with management guiding to mid-30s for FY27.
summary.overview:
Consolidated revenue from operations was Rs.141.6 Cr, down from Rs.178.1 Cr in Q4 FY26 and Rs.158.2 Cr in Q1 FY26, which management attributed to order execution timing. Operational EBITDA was Rs.38.7 Cr at a 27.3% margin versus 40.9% a year ago and 28.6% in Q4, with management citing negative operating leverage on a largely fixed cost base and a Rs.7.65 Cr provision release in the prior-year quarter. Reported PAT was Rs.34.5 Cr after a Rs.3.4 Cr exceptional fire-related loss at a subsidiary; adjusted PAT is about Rs.37 Cr (26.1% margin). Order book stood at Rs.1,239 Cr, with a Rs.177.5 Cr Ministry of Defence simulator order received after quarter end; the group remains debt free with about Rs.1,217 Cr cash.</overview>

segments.name: Simulators (army, navy, air force)
segments.commentary: Management calls simulators and anti-drone systems the two matured franchises; a Rs.177.5 Cr MoD order for tank and crew gunnery simulator upgradation came after quarter end. Management expects Rs.700-800 Cr of simulator orders in the pipeline, with some possibly within months.

segments.name: Anti-drone / counter-drone systems
segments.commentary: Demand is tender-gated: management says no anti-drone or simulator tenders have been floated recently, though a fast-track process is expected to bring them. Management cited about Rs.800 Cr of anti-drone orders after Operation Sindoor and expects anti-drone opportunities of at least Rs.2,000 Cr.

segments.name: Vector Technics (drone propulsion)
segments.commentary: Capacity expanded to about 300,000 units. Management said drone segment orders have slowed; it estimates Rs.300 Cr potential revenue if orders at Rs.10,000 per unit materialise, with about 50% of enquiries from overseas.

segments.name: Robotics / new products
segments.commentary: Vrishabh unmanned ground vehicle has completed internal trials; customer trials pending. Management expects robotics, autonomous vehicles and related products to take at least two to three years to mature.

guidance_outlook: FY27 full-year operational EBITDA margin expected in the mid-30s, as revenue scales and operating leverage works in the company's favour; Q1 margin was below the 35% guidance.
Order book expected to end FY27 at about Rs.2,500 Cr after FY27 execution, per management's earlier investor-meeting communication.
Revenue for FY27 expected to be weighted toward Q2 and Q3, given that much of the order book was secured in H2 FY26 with roughly 12-month execution cycles.
Management referenced a cumulative Rs.4,000 Cr revenue target for FY27 and FY28 combined; the simulator share was put at about Rs.2,000 Cr.
Management said it is actively looking to acquire companies, with funds remaining from QIP plus accumulated cash.
capex_capacity: Vector Technics propulsion capacity expanded to about 300,000 units.
Working capital build-up in supplier advances and inventory to execute order book deliveries through FY27.

Air Force: first flight simulator (C295 referred to on the call as C195 in one answer) developed in-house; full motion simulator capability available; company shortlisted for future Air Force simulators.
demand_pricing: Q1 order intake was Rs.44.6 Cr against Rs.141.6 Cr executed, so the order book declined from March 2026.

Management attributes softness to demand, not supply: no tenders for anti-drone or simulator systems had been issued recently; prior tenders were single-vendor because competitors were disqualified on technical grounds.
Management expects some competition and says Zen will not win every requirement.

Export push: targeting Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia and CIS; also North America and EU via prime contractors (FOCI and ITAR clearances in progress). Management says US target is about $100 Mn in year three.
Government is moving more orders to 12-month fast-track procurement (FTP) cycles, though large orders still go through regular procurement.
